title: Biomodel Engineering of Unilevel to Multilevel Biological Models Using Colored Petri Nets
author: Liu, Heiner, et al.
materials: Timing: hours to months based on model's complexity
Timing: hours to days based on model's complexity

steps.title: Define problem and requirements
steps.instruction: Write a clear problem statement, set system boundaries, choose model levels (e.g., cell, tissue, organ) and any spatial relationships, and record all in a detailed Problem Description & Requirements Specification document.

steps.title: Collect biological information
steps.instruction: Gather all relevant literature and database information about the biological system, including spatial relationships, needed for the multilevel model.

steps.title: Analyze system and design model
steps.instruction: Determine the number and names of levels, components at each level, and connections between levels; decide how instances are organized within and between levels (linear, tree, or acyclic graph) and define spatial arrangements (e.g., hexagonal cells, Cartesian 2‑D space).

steps.title: Create component models
steps.instruction: Using Snoopy’s graphical editor, construct each component (e.g., biochemical reaction network, cellular compartment) with appropriate colors to encode levels, space, and repeated entities.

steps.title: Animate component (token game)
steps.instruction: Open the View menu, select “Start Anim‑mode”, launch the animation dialog, then click “Play forward” for continuous animation or repeatedly click “Step forward” for manual stepping to observe token flow.

steps.title: Component structural analysis
steps.instruction: Export the Snoopy model to ANDL format, load it into Charlie, and run (a) elementary graph property check, (b) place‑ and transition‑invariant computation, and (c) Siphon‑Trap Property analysis, exporting results if desired.

substeps.instruction: Open the bar “net properties” to view elementary graph results (green = YES, red = NO).
For invariants: click the “IM‑based analysis” bar, choose structural boundedness, P‑invariant or T‑invariant, set export options, then click Compute.
For STP: click the “siphon/trap computation” bar, select siphons, traps, or STP, enable “compute all” if needed, set export options, then click Compute.

steps.title: Component simulation
steps.instruction: In Snoopy, select View → “Start Simulation‑Mode”, configure model marking, rate functions and constants, set simulation interval and observation points, choose a simulator type (see Table 2), define result views, run the simulation, observe traces, and export results to CSV or image files.

substeps.instruction: Model configuration: choose marking set, rate function set, constant values.
Simulation configuration: set start/end times, number of observation points, select algorithm (e.g., Gillespie, Tau‑leaping, Euler, BDF, HRSSA, etc.) and its properties.
Views: add or remove views, edit node list (select places/transitions by name or regex).
Run simulation by clicking “Start Simulation” and monitor the progress bar.
After completion, double‑click a view to inspect traces.
Export selected results as CSV (choose separator) or as image (png, jpeg, …).

steps.title: Component dynamic analysis
steps.instruction: Validate simulation behavior by (a) model checking with Marcie or MC2, (b) time‑series data analytics, and (c) cross‑validation against experimental data.

substeps.instruction: Model checking: ensure an ANDL (or CANDL) file exists; write CTL/CSL/PLTL queries in a text file; run commands such as `marcie --net-file=GeneGate.andl --ctl-file=properties.ctl` or `marcie --net-file=GeneGate.andl --csl-file=transient.csl --const=k=10,t1=1,t2=1`; for MC2 use `java -jar MC2Tool.jar traces.csv property.queries -time -snoopy`.
Time‑series analytics: load CSV traces into MATLAB, R or similar and apply standard statistical or machine‑learning methods.
Cross‑validation: repeatedly split data into training and test sets to avoid over‑fitting.

steps.title: Component optimization
steps.instruction: Adjust kinetic rate constants by manual exploration or automated parameter scanning with Spike (SPC file), or apply target‑driven heuristics (hill climbing, simulated annealing, genetic algorithms) via external harnesses linked to Spike; modify constants directly in the ANDL or SPC file.

substeps.instruction: Define scanning ranges and intervals carefully; run Spike scans.
For heuristic optimization, configure the chosen algorithm and execute it, updating the model files as needed.

steps.title: Store component in library
steps.instruction: Save component files (ANDL, CANDL, Snoopy XML) in a designated folder or database, use version control (e.g., Git) to track changes, and keep the uncompressed XML format for graphical layout preservation.

steps.title: System animation (colored nets)
steps.instruction: Open View → “Start Anim‑mode” for a colored Petri net, choose an unfolding method (IDD‑based, Gecode‑based, or Generic), click “Start” in the unfolding dialog, then run the animation (Play forward or Step forward) on the automatically unfolded net.

substeps.instruction: In manual mode, clicking a transition opens a binding selection dialog to choose a firing binding.

steps.title: System structural analysis
steps.instruction: Export the colored model to ANDL (which triggers unfolding), load the unfolded model into Charlie, and repeat the elementary graph, invariant, and STP analyses as described for components; be aware that the unfolded model may be large and require a separate computer.

steps.title: System simulation
steps.instruction: Start Simulation‑Mode for a colored net; an unfolding dialog appears—select the same unfolding method as in animation, then configure simulation parameters (interval, points, algorithm) and views, run the simulation, and export results as CSV or images.

substeps.instruction: In the view window, use “Edit Node List” to select colored or uncolored places/transitions (manual selection, advanced dropdown, or regex).

steps.title: System dynamic analysis
steps.instruction: Perform (a) simulative model checking on the unfolded system using Marcie or MC2 with queries that reference unfolded place names, (b) time‑series analytics on exported CSV traces, and (c) visualisation of 2‑D/3‑D patterns or movies using provided Python scripts.

substeps.instruction: Model checking: write queries (e.g., `P>=1[ F(G([NI_x_y] > 9 ^ [D_x_y] < 1) ) ]`) and run Marcie/MC2 as in component analysis.
2‑D plot: export relevant traces, edit `2DHexagonPlot.py` with file name and separator, run the script to generate the plot.
2‑D movie: export diffusion traces, edit `2DMovie.py` with file name, separator, grid size, run to produce the movie.

steps.title: System optimization
steps.instruction: Adjust kinetic parameters and neighborhood expressions to match reference spatial‑temporal patterns; repeat simulations until the desired phenotype is obtained, preferably using automated target‑driven optimization rather than exhaustive scanning.
